newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire break-up could be catching - Madagascar leader.
newsitem.headline: Zaire break-up could be catching - Madagascar leader.

text.p: The president of Madagascar warned on Monday that if Zaire were to break up, Nigeria and other African countries could follow suit.

"Zaire must not be abandoned, otherwise it's an open door to adventurism. Nigeria will follow and other countries too...We're not going to start another Rwanda in Zaire," President Didier Ratsiraka told reporters after talks with his French counterpart Jacques Chirac.
"We must settle things as soon as possible to prevent (the troubles) spreading," he added.
"It would be a pity to let a country like Zaire be taken to bits. Federal solutions may be considered but it would be a pity to drop Zaire."

Rebels seeking the overthrow of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko have seized a 1,000-km (650-mile) border strip of eastern Zaire and say they have surrounded the city of Kisangani, from where the Zairean army is coordinating its counter-offensive.
The radio station run by the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL), said the government was deserting Kisangani.
Fleeing the rebels, tens of thousands of Rwandan refugees, possibly as many as 100,000, flooded into the eastern Zairean town of Ubundu over the weekend, the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said.
The Tingi Tingi camp was abandoned by its 170,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees 10 days ago, shortly before it fell to the rebels.
